description.narrative: The Protracted Crises Recovery Assistance (PCRA) investment will provide recovery, rehabilitation, and reconstruction support required for protracted crises and other large-scale disasters. The investment will cover agreements that provide long-term assistance to address the needs of displaced families, households, and communities, especially women and children, persons with disabilities, and older people in vulnerable situations. Activities include protection and social support services, durable housing, policy development, sustainable and climate-resilient livelihoods, and support to displaced families to reduce vulnerabilities to future shocks.

description.narrative: In 2024, the Resilient Livelihoods Development for Women and Youth Internally Displaced Persons in Maguindanao (RLD) project provided 1,510 women with agriculture-based livelihood assistance and food processing equipment. Through hands-on training, participants established small businesses producing local products such as chili garlic condiments and banana/sweet potato/mushroom chips. The women established 28 community-based organizations and registered with the BARMM Ministry of Labor and Employment, enabling them to access government programs and formal markets locally and abroad. The project also supported the development of online platforms (e.g., Facebook Marketplace) to expand market reach, boost sales, and connect with local buyers. ‍ Salha Salik, a member of the East Libutan Women and Youth Producer Association, shared that she no longer needed to seek work abroad to fund her college education. The initiative had instead helped her earn an income by producing water spinach chips. She used this income to pay for her school tuition and graduated Cum Laude – breaking the glass ceiling for young Muslim women in BARMM.

The ‘Promoting Local Recovery and Resilience: We Can Project’ (WCP) aims to assist 6,000 households affected by Super Typhoon Rai (local name: Odette) in the provinces of Dinagat Islands, Surigao del Norte, and Southern Leyte. The project supported climate-resilient and sustainable livelihoods; reduced community vulnerability to future shocks through local disaster risk reduction efforts; facilitated access to government social protection programmes; and strengthened community-based mental health and psychosocial support systems. ‍ In 2023, WCP reached more than 657 individuals with household-based livelihood support – including 289 women entrepreneurs who received cash assistance through their participation in cash-for-work activities (e.g., vegetable gardening, rehabilitation of community assets, preparation for livelihood activity, etc). They also received start-up capital (cash or goods) for their businesses. Some of the women entrepreneurs expanded their skills to produce more high-quality products (i.e. woven bags, etc) which they sell at local markets.

Through the Resilient Livelihoods Development joint program of UNFPA and FAO, Australia trained 74 women and girls to be women-friendly space (WFS) facilitators. The WFS facilitators provides support to ensure gender-based violence (GBV) survivors have a safe space to access information on sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) and multi-sectoral services (e.g., medical, psychosocial) through a referral mechanism. ‍ For the Severe Tropical Storm Nalgae response, WFS facilitators conducted an awareness-raising session on GBV and SRHR at an evacuation center in Kusiong Elementary School reaching 30 displaced pregnant and nursing women and adolescent girls.

Under the ‘Promoting Local Recovery and Resilience: We Can Project’ (WCP), Australia in partnership with Community and Family Services International (CFSI) supported the Bajau (sea nomads) Indigenous community in Surigao del Norte whose houses and livelihoods were heavily affected by Super Typhoon Rai (local name: Odette) in 2021. ‍ CFSI engaged the Bajau community in backyard vegetable gardening aimed to improve their food security and serve as an alternative source of income. The local government complemented the WCP by providing agricultural inputs (i.e. seeds, compost soil) and conducting training to enhance their gardening skills.
